question_text: Recent research has highlighted a dose-response relationship between social media use and depression. Which of the following experimental designs would best elucidate the causal mechanisms underlying this relationship?

C) An ecological momentary assessment study measuring real-time social media use and mood fluctuations
D) A randomized controlled trial manipulating social media use and measuring depressive symptoms
rationale: While a randomized controlled trial (D) could establish causality, an ecological momentary assessment (EMA) study (C) would be best suited to elucidate the causal mechanisms underlying the relationship between social media use and depression. EMA involves repeated sampling of subjects' current behaviors and experiences in real time, in their natural environments. This method could capture the immediate effects of social media use on mood, as well as potential mediating factors (e.g., social comparison, fear of missing out) that may explain the dose-response relationship. It allows for a more nuanced understanding of how, when, and why social media use might lead to depressive symptoms, providing insights into the underlying mechanisms that a traditional RCT might miss.
